summary: Relic Rangers is a concept for an interactive storytelling experience that helps students aged 8 to 14 discover the machines NASA has left behind on the Moon, Mars and in deep space. Each machine, such as the Apollo Lunar Rover, Sojourner, Ingenuity and Voyager 1, becomes a character with a story card, a real NASA photo and a timeline. A Story Map shows where each machine rests, and simple Trade-Off Games let students balance mass, power and science instruments the way real engineers do. The project answers the challenge by turning “discarded equipment” into living history and making engineering trade-offs tangible and fun. It matters because it can spark curiosity in young learners and help them see that every mission leaves a legacy.
details:
What it does: Relic Rangers has three parts: a Story Map of the Moon and Mars, Story Cards with real NASA photos, and Trade-Off Games where students balance mass, power and science.

Benefits and impact: Students learn why engineers leave hardware behind and what trade-offs shaped each mission.

Tools: Canva for the presentation. Claude (Anthropic) for developing the concept and drafting the content.
